reason: Conversation 1 went straight to the sensible first step (thermostat setting and food against the rear vent), got the key facts in one exchange, gave correct part-free advice, suggested a thermometer, and handled the follow-up honestly by treating one residual yoghurt at the coldest spot as expected while defining clear 'when to worry' criteria pointing to a damper fault and engineer. Conversation 2 opened with an unnecessary 'switch it off and unplug it', anchored on an unsupported evaporator-icing/defrost-fault theory (which doesn't fit a normally working freezer and a 3-year-old frost-free unit), pushed a disruptive full manual defrost before asking about the obvious causes, took three turns to reach the vent question and never asked about the dial until the customer volunteered it. Its final answer wrongly attributes residual freezing to 'holding onto cold air' and again steers toward a defrost rather than a damper/thermostat check, and it never mentioned a thermometer or a clear escalation path.
